newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish pilots sacked for cockpit punchup.
newsitem.headline: Turkish pilots sacked for cockpit punchup.

text.p: Turkish Airlines (THY) said on Monday it had sacked two pilots who had a punch-up in the cockpit of a THY passenger plane on a flight between Bangkok and Istanbul.

"Immediately after the incident, which took place on April 4, 1997, the THY administration took action and stopped the flights of captain pilots Altan Tezcan and Erdogan Gecim and sent them to the disciplinary board," THY said in a statement.
"The THY executive board, which met today, has annulled the contracts of the two pilots in question," it said.

Turkish newspapers on Monday reported the incident, which they said had taken place because of an apparent misunderstanding by Tezcan of altitude instructions by the control tower 45 minutes after take-off from Bangkok.
Around 240 passengers were travelling on the Airbus 340 plane, according to Sabah newspaper.

Yeni Yuzyil daily quoted Gecim as telling Tezcan: "Are you deaf? He's telling you something and you are doing something completely different." The paper said Gecim then rapped Tezcan's knuckles as he tried to programme the data into the auto-pilot.
The pair then untied their belts for a fisticuffs, which was only ended with the intervention of other staff. A third, more junior pilot completed the flight, newspapers said.
